title: Affective Calculus · Why read this book?

narrator.label: Narrator
narrator.description: An articulate adult English narrator with warm authority and a thoughtful, varied cadence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Affective Calculus asks whether an AI can explain an emotion, not merely name it.

direction.delivery: Open with a confident, curious lift on 'explain'.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A character can say “I’m perfectly fine” in a scene of despair.

direction.delivery: Soften; let the quoted words land with gentle irony.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An AI judge hunting for emotion words mistakes that expression for the actual state.

direction.delivery: Steady and precise, a slight frown in the voice.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book treats emotion as an evaluated relationship between an agent and its world.

direction.delivery: Settle warmly, as a clear definition.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its proposed Appraisal Affective Calculus first separates brief episodes from moods, sentiments and attitudes.

direction.delivery: Measured pace; give each category its own small beat.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An appraisal vector then records goals, control, agency, norms, dignity and attachment.

direction.delivery: Slightly brighter, listing dimensions with even rhythm.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Labels become probabilistic prototypes, with intensity and confidence reported separately.

direction.delivery: Calm and exact, a light emphasis on 'separately'.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mara faces a running dog, a locked gate and a dead-end alley: fear.

direction.delivery: Quicker and tighter, then a short pause before 'fear'.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Now she can shut the gate, and the owner freed the dog deliberately: anger should rise.

direction.delivery: Shift tone decisively on 'anger', firm but not loud.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Such minimal pairs reveal whether an AI explains emotion or only matches words.

direction.delivery: Slow down; let the distinction register.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Read it for that test, starting with Chapter 1, “An Emotion Is Not a Word.”

direction.delivery: Warm, direct invitation, unhurried on the chapter title.
